shell-injected-env: The sidecar process this TS ran in carried GAMELIB_SHELL_EXE, GAMELIB_APP_ROOT, GAMELIB_STEAM_ROOT_DEFAULT and GAMELIB_STORE_BOOT, injected by src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs. A spawn from the shell own environment does not carry them, so the Rust runner env is the golden env without those four keys. No golden here holds them (the cases run on the pinned base env), so the Rust side adds none and the delta only records the rule for the cases that compare against a sidecar-run recording.
caller-arrays-mutated: The TS runWineCommand changes the arrays its caller handed it: commandParts gains the proton verb, the wrappers and the runner bin in place, and options.wrappers loses its first element to the spawned binary (commandPartsAfter, wrappersAfter in result.json). The Rust function takes its arguments by value and builds the argv on its own copy, so the Rust side compares the spawned argv and leaves both lists as the caller had them.
error-stack-trace: A launch script that fails to spawn is logged by runScriptForGame as the Error itself, and the TS log writer stringifies it with its JS stack (frames naming src/backend files and node_modules). The golden keeps the first line, "Error: spawn <script> <code>", and drops the "    at ..." lines, which name the machine and the test runner. The Rust runner logs the spawn error message and has no JS stack, so the comparison is on the first line only.
game-merged-streams: A game-class wine command (the runner.wine_command.launch cases) writes both of its output streams to one capture file that Rust tails, so Rust cannot tell stdout from stderr and reads in chunks of its own. The replay compares a game case with: the chunks the observer saw and the raw entries written to one log writer joined into the one text they make (the header entry never joins and is compared on its own, before any output); and a result that ended on its own answering the whole printed text as stdout with no stderr. The order and count of every other entry, the spawn (program, argv, env, cwd, class, timeout), the tracked key, the general log lines and the exit code are compared as recorded. This is the same delta golden/runner carries for the runner.call.launch cases.
helper-spawn-not-reported: The spawn seam of a helper-class run does not report that the child started or its pid. The TS wrote the Wine Command header from onSpawn, before any output; the Rust helper arm writes it with the first chunk or, for a command that printed nothing, when the child ends, and not at all for a spawn that failed (the order the log shows is the recorded one: header, then output). onSpawn is a TS callback that is handed the child handle and has no wire form: the one recorded case that sets it (a helper-class command) is compared on everything but the callback count, and the game arm reports the pid to the output sink (runnerSpawned). hasSignal (the TS signal option) is not compared: every Rust run carries a cancel token, which the TS runner did not.
